The trace reaches the first held segment and records USR completion before fault 6. It contains no 256-byte comparison or successful return. The key question is whether SLV_END reports the controller FSM finishing while KEEP still holds CS low; I’m also checking the matched flash’s READ03 timing limit.

The frozen core clears and verifies SLV_END before launch, so the observed bit is fresh; MST_END may be older. The S31 comments describe both an FSM-end event and a KEEP override, which makes “SLV_END means the physical CS pin rose” an unproven inference here. The next read must preserve event freshness checks while collecting the continuation data.

The flash timing check needs the correct part family: the recorded ID is `46:4018`. XMC’s matching XM25UH128D datasheet allows READ03 at 80 MHz under its stated conditions, so a generic 50 MHz limit would be unjustified. The board’s exact revision and electrical conditions remain unverified; this does not establish read correctness. [XMC datasheet](https://www.xmcwh.com/uploads/1045/XM25UH128D_Ver1.2.pdf)

A bounded four-segment read can test continuation without treating SLV_END as a pin measurement. It must record each segment’s event before clearing it, retain the USR timeout and command restrictions, and still require all 256 bytes plus register restoration to match. Root’s journal now records the full original-flash comparison complete at 12:36:30 UTC.

The linked fault branch tests bit 3 and stops before copying the first segment’s FIFO data. That rules out interpreting this run as a data mismatch or DRAM/cache failure. A later full four-quarter match would provide evidence of functional READ continuation, while leaving physical CS continuity and PP behavior unproven.

Decision: fresh SLV_END with KEEP=1 does **not directly prove physical CS rose**. Recommend one bounded four-segment READ with recorded events and verified clearing before each launch, retaining command restrictions, guards, timeouts, all-256-byte comparison, restoration checks and protected failure handling.
